target.name: XMOS
target.founder: Ali Dixon, James Foster, Noel Hurley, David May, Hitesh Mehta

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $200M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
XMOS is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised £200M+ to date. The comparable universe in Chips & Semiconductors comprises 12 same-sector peers (3 public: ALAB, NVDA, AMD; 8 private including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched), though narrow peer matching proved constrained.

Of three valuation methods tested, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the £200M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage progression, yielding £240M. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting the minimum threshold of three datapoints within the narrow semiconductor segment. Public-Comp Anchoring, while supported by a 21.0x P/S median across the three public semiconductors, could not be applied because XMOS revenue is not on file—standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of £204M to £276M, with a median of £240M derived solely from the Stage-Progression method. The single-method result reflects the thinness of comparable data. Key uncertainties include XMOS's actual revenue run-rate and detailed stage indicators relative to the private peer set, either of which would enable peer-median or public-anchor methodologies and materially strengthen conviction in the range.
